scope: Final visible Draft, exact source/article/action/deployed bytes, core package-env and NAS planning PRs, full Fleet Runner gate discussion, complete daily-logger review-PR inventory, workstation-yuri #12 lifecycle, current review schema/discovery and held-candidate custody. Read-only review; no article revision or acceptance, finding disposition, action admission or settlement, readiness, merge, workflow dispatch, runtime, or scheduling authority.

findings.title: The package-env contract is not a sole-source env-file rule
findings.location: Line 31 says the package .env file is the sole configuration source and deviations are violations; line 69 calls the convention established.
findings.explanation: PR #598 allows real environment variables to override the file, keeps *_FILE secret paths, and makes one settings module the environment-reading boundary. Its ADR remains a draft, existing packages migrate later, and the current guard emits expected migration warnings.
findings.correction: Describe #598 as a proposed package-settings boundary with one untracked file, allowed environment and secret-file overrides, one settings module, and pending migration and ADR acceptance.

findings.title: G7 already had owners and active qualification
findings.location: Line 51 erases G7 ownership and sequencing; lines 67 through 69 say G7 cannot be sequenced until the #590/#595 relationship is answered.
findings.explanation: The conductor records G7 as separately owned, with dedicated recovery and restored-generation owners. Actual restore qualification had already exposed a defect, applied its reviewed fix and restored a held database before #595 opened. #595 preserves current conductor owners and requires later sequencing reconciliation; it does not gate G7.
findings.correction: Keep the #590/#595 relationship as an unresolved account-migration design question, but report G7 as separately owned and already in qualification; do not block it without a new owner decision.

findings.title: The article-review queue inventory is wrong
findings.location: Lines 53, 67 and 69 list nine independent audits, include #531 and say the oldest dates to November 3.
findings.explanation: Ten review-only Draft PRs were open: #515, #524, #526, #529, #530, #533, #535, #537, #539 and #541. The oldest, #515, opened October 31. #531 changes telemetry code and instructions rather than review data.
findings.correction: Report ten open review-data Draft PRs, oldest #515 from October 31, remove #531 from the set, and use that exact set for any triage candidate.

findings.title: workstation-yuri PR 12 had already merged
findings.location: Lines 57 and 69 call #12 non-draft, awaiting owner review and separated from closure only by an owner pull event.
findings.explanation: PR #12 merged at 2026-11-12T02:13:02Z, more than a day before the article capture. Its checks and pre-merge owner-review wording were historical by generation time.
findings.correction: Report #12 as merged and remove it from open or merge-ready work and from retained action context.

findings.title: No public record makes PR 598 a prerequisite for PR 597
findings.location: Line 67 says #598 is a prerequisite discipline for #597 deployment and that no implementation is authorized until both close.
findings.explanation: PR #597 requires operator wording review and reconciliation with conductor sequencing. PR #598 says existing packages migrate later and Selfco workers adopt the convention when they move. Neither record binds #597 review, implementation or deployment to #598 closing first.
findings.correction: Present #597 and #598 as separate pending owner reviews unless the owner records an explicit dependency and entrance criterion.

findings.title: The detailed workstation-home failure mechanism is unsupported
findings.location: Line 37 says the services resolve relative to the operator home and silently fail on remote SSH, an unmounted home or a different effective user.
findings.explanation: PR #595 establishes the public requirement to replace workstation-home dependencies and qualify restart without login, permissions, recovery and rollback. Its public handoff omits the private audit and does not establish the article's three specific current failure scenarios.
findings.correction: Use the documented rationale of removing workstation-home and login dependencies, or link a publishable primary receipt that proves the specific path-resolution and failure behavior.
